scope: Test-only memory retention and potential process partitioning; no production, assertion, timeout, cache or canonical shard changes.

findings.finding: Process-global caches retain distinct analyzer inputs and results without a capacity or per-fixture lifetime bound.
findings.details: Sixteen sync.Map cache declarations are present. Parsed ASTs are keyed by path plus source hash; type graphs and models are keyed by source/graph/projection fingerprints. The graph-cache deletion handles stale inputs, not bounded retention of distinct mutations. No bulk/lifetime Clear was found.
findings.confidence_limit: The source establishes reachability/lifetime behavior, not how many bytes each cache owns in a particular run.

findings.finding: A small source mutation can create another package-wide typed graph, not just a small changed-file object.
findings.details: Graphs retain parsed package files, go/types information and loaded source strings. Missing production package files are augmented from disk. Models retain typed packages and multiple AST/object/type maps.

findings.finding: Clearing only the top-level model cache would not remove all retention paths.
findings.details: Binding-cache keys retain model and function pointers. Stable-expression cache keys retain AST expressions; initialization bindings also retain expressions. Garbage collection cannot reclaim objects that remain reachable from these caches.

findings.finding: Existing cache correctness contracts must survive any lifetime optimization.
findings.details: Tests require same-input model reuse, mutation-sensitive invalidation, projection distinctions, caller-copy isolation and one immutable contract-baseline build. An indiscriminate reset or weakened key is not an acceptable memory fix.

findings.finding: Top-level process splits can reduce accumulated state, but cannot solve every large test.
findings.details: Rev-19 and rev-20 currently share a process and each builds multiple mutated models. The purge-progress guard already runs alone yet loops through many model variants inside one PIB-518 subtest; simply running each top-level test separately cannot partition those internal loops.

findings.finding: Canonical sharding has enforced CI and coverage parity.
findings.details: Any adopted partition change must update the CI commands, local script, exact-order/coverage guards and dependent profiler selection together. Experimental selection must not be presented as full canonical coverage.

recommended_next_measurement.constraints: Explicitly authorize a bounded experiment before running it. Freeze source/Go version, preserve test timeouts, retain private profiles, and do not change caches or canonical CI/shards.
recommended_next_measurement.next_decision: If top-level splits reduce the peak sufficiently, validate complete non-overlapping coverage and runtime cost. If individual tests remain large, investigate a scoped analyzer-cache lifetime using heap evidence.

not_recommended_without_more_evidence: Treating GOMEMLIMIT or more frequent GC as an eviction mechanism for strongly reachable caches
Clearing only s6TypeModelCache while dependent caches still retain models/ASTs
Resetting the immutable contract baseline or bypassing cache-sensitivity assertions
Claiming a guaranteed old-Mac memory target from static inspection or a subset's RSS
